data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 names a 'reduction' relation but mis-identifies what is reduced: it claims 015994869366 'inherits from SRC_001,' then says the inherited target (genuine reliability) 'reduces to the frozen mapping's causal completeness.' But SRC_001's reliability claim is about aggregation of independent micro-decisions via a Condorcet-style mechanism, not about the checklist's causal completeness. Causal completeness of the checklist is a different property from step-conditional independence of panel errors, which SRC_001 itself flags as a countercondition. So the proposed reduction changes the subject from aggregation-mechanism reliability to mapping-completeness reliability without establishing that the former reduces to the latter. The 'refuted if' clause is also mis-specified: it says refuted if any single-evaluation method uniquely determines causal completeness without cross-distribution testing — but that is a claim about epistemic access to completeness, not about whether the reduction from panel reliability to causal completeness holds.
